findings.title: Recovery codes are written to user storage in plaintext
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generatedCodes list to JSON and passes it as the credential data to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). The local-storage path instead stores a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel built from the same codes, which is designed to hold hashed codes (RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode exists for this). External user storage providers therefore receive and persist usable plaintext recovery codes, which a storage backend or anyone with read access to it can use to bypass MFA. The user-storage branch should store hashed codes, matching the local representation, and verification should compare hashes.

findings.title: Recovery codes in user storage are never consumed after use
findings.body: isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks membership in the stored list and never removes or marks the used code. In local storage each code is single-use, so a code entered once can be entered again here indefinitely. The test provider also has no test asserting that a used code is rejected, so this gap is not caught. The provider's contract should require consuming the code, or the code should be documented as a limitation.

findings.title: Credential id is dropped when recovery codes are returned from getCredentials
findings.body: updateCredential assigns a generated id to recoveryCodesModel, but getCredentials rebuilds the model with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...), which does not copy that id. The returned credential therefore has no id matching the stored one. The authenticator then calls removeStoredCredentialById with that id once all codes are used, so the removal targets a non-existent credential and the spent codes remain stored.

findings.title: Removal of exhausted codes does not work for user-storage credentials
findings.body: getCredential now returns federated (user storage) credentials first, but the removal call at line 86 uses credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(), which only operates on local-storage credentials. When the exhausted codes come from user storage, nothing is removed. The exhausted credential stays in storage, and getCredential keeps finding it on later logins. The removal should go through a path that handles federated credentials, or the mismatch should be handled explicitly.

findings.title: Unguarded Optional.get() when no recovery credential exists
findings.body: The constructor calls credentialModelOpt.get() without checking isPresent(). If the user has no recovery credential in either storage, this throws NoSuchElementException during page rendering instead of producing a controlled error.
